items.title: Randy Sandke interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 10, 1997
items.q: So I spent $9,000 of my own on a concert, and Mike Brecker was there, Chris Potter — I put together a great band

ctx.x: Yeah. Which is not to say — the way it works, that part of my career, it’s like this part of my career, I have a good time, I love these guys, I love playing the music and I make money and every year, I mean the jobs are fine. I mean here we are in this nice hotel. But for doing the other kind of stuff, it means using the money I make for that too, to like finance a concert, finance a record, finance this or that. And it gets increasingly hard for me to do, especially if I do that I mean just to give you one…

tried, or he tried to get himself over as this “downtown scene” musician, avoiding the label jazz, avoiding the comparisons with Coltrane and the young lions and the black and white thing and whatever — he just sidesteps that and he finds his audience and he gets his — he establishes his way. And I’m kind of finding the same thing. If I try to promote this as jazz you run up into a million hurdles from all kinds of directions. If I on the other hand go into a contemporary classical music direction I find that…
